summary: Documented step M1-S03 (tested -> documented) in build tier2-webhook after three consecutive S 4 test-only repairs (runs 6-8, closing S2-F-14/15/16) and the org's whole-build validation at run 12 (37/37 tests, 89.9% coverage, no coverage warnings, reports/MOCK-DEPLOY-M1.md). Re-rendered PLAN.md and CLARIFICATIONS.md. Appended three decisions to decisions.md, one per repair: D-M1S03-13 (the Tier2WebhookFinalizer stub-testing technique, UNVERIFIED at run 6's S6-F-02, confirmed by the org at run 7's S7-F-02, plus the one-line mock fix run 7 needed for a method the re-enqueued job executed regardless of Test.startTest()/Test.stopTest() wrapping), D-M1S03-14 (the per-class 75% coverage floor Apex's RunSpecifiedTests enforces separately from the aggregate, and the two Tier2EscalationServiceTest branch methods that closed it for S2-F-16), and D-M1S03-15 (Tier2WebhookFinalizerTest as a new ApexClass member M1-S05's manifest must add -- recorded as an obligation being resolved in a parallel M1-S05 re-run this pass does not touch, per this pass's own instructions). Updated exactly one traceability.md row in place: REQ-013, the only row whose artefact_paths cell names Tier2WebhookFinalizer.cls, gains artefacts/M1-S03/classes/Tier2WebhookFinalizerTest.cls and a test_result note correcting its prior 'deliberately uncovered' framing for the Finalizer's own retry/abandon/update decision logic, which is now directly unit-tested (the live throw -> Finalizer chain itself remains correctly described as undriveable by any test, for the reason that row already gave). Also refreshed the file's own 'Coverage notes' section: a new top note documents this pass and demotes the prior M1-S04 note to a superseded subsection, following this file's own established convention. check_rtm.py re-run after the edit: 16 rows, build schema, 0 coverage gaps, 0 orphans, 0 errors, 0 warnings -- unchanged from before this pass's edit, confirming the row edit introduced no new gap or orphan. Workbook untouched: scale: feature keeps the ten-section workbook optional (standards/build-orchestration.md section 3.1), and this build has never populated one across eight prior documentation passes -- this pass keeps that precedent per its own explicit instruction. No file under artefacts/M1-S05/ or any of M1-S05's own workbook/traceability rows was touched.
confidence_rationale: MEDIUM per Step 11's per-step table: no artefact this pass wrote lacked a source_req_id or a verification step, and re-running check_rtm.py before and after the edit confirms no duplicate or orphan was introduced -- that alone would read HIGH. Held at MEDIUM for two reasons carried forward from this same step's prior documentation passes and one new to this pass: (1) M1-S05's build-level package.xml remains confirmed stale -- it still lists the pre-run-6 thirteen ApexClass members, not the fourteen this step now ships, an obligation D-M1S03-15 records but does not close, deliberately left to a parallel M1-S05 re-run per this pass's own instructions; (2) this design-only build still has no offline Apex compiler (agents/_shared/AGENT_CONTRACT.md, Gate C), so every fact this pass states about the three repairs' correctness rests on reports/MOCK-DEPLOY-M1.md's org evidence (runs 9-12), supplied as input to this pass rather than produced or independently re-verified by it; (3) scoping the traceability edit to REQ-013 alone -- the one row naming Tier2WebhookFinalizer.cls, the production class the new test class directly unit-tests -- rather than also touching REQ-011/REQ-012 (whose artefact_paths already name Tier2EscalationServiceTest.cls, which gained two new methods from a different repair, S2-F-16, not the new test class this pass's own instructions scoped it to) was a judgment call, recorded in this pass's Process Observations as ambiguous rather than settled by the task's own wording alone.

The org's own run 12 (SOURCE mode, --test-level RunSpecifiedTests: 37/37 tests, 89.9% coverage, no coverage warnings) independently confirms the closure of all three findings this pass documents (S2-F-14, S2-F-15, S2-F-16), so the decisions and the traceability update rest on executed-test evidence rather than on the repairing agent's own reasoning alone.
